description:
Coverage loss named by fz-go4.18.9's intent-preservation audit (2026-07-02). The retargeted suspend-continuation test deleted assert_no_unreachable_callable_facts + collect_callable_shapes (sole caller, verified). The deletion RATIONALE is sound: the helper's shapes-only reachability model false-positives on callables that are legitimately justified only through boxed arrow-typed lanes (the continuation inside an un-destructured suspend tuple; the generic boxed-apply carrier at a cont.() call) -- structural ShapeDescr::Callable children are not the only justification path in the demand-driven product.

But the PROPERTY is now untested everywhere: if callable_facts_inventory regressed to accumulating orphaned/unjustified callable facts (garbage entries no boundary, no shape child, and no arrow-typed lane justifies), nothing would catch it. That's the produced-but-unread disease at the product level.

TASK: build a LANE-AWARE reachability model for callable-facts justification -- a callable fact is justified if reachable from (a) a structural ShapeDescr::Callable child of any recorded transport shape, (b) a boundary's callable, or (c) an arrow-typed lane whose Ty's callable resolution set names it (the boxed-value path the old model missed). Assert inventory ⊆ justified on a fixture family that exercises all three justification paths (the fz-go4.18.9 suspend fixture pair covers (c); pick simple direct-callable fixtures for (a)/(b)). Wire it as a reusable test helper, re-adopt it in the suspend-continuation test (restoring the stronger form of what was deleted), and consider adopting it in 1-2 other transport-contract tests where the inventory is small enough to enumerate.

ACCEPTANCE: helper exists with the three-path justification model; suspend test re-asserts no-unjustified-facts and stays green; a deliberate-garbage negative test (inject a fact nothing justifies, assert the helper catches it) proves the helper is non-vacuous; suite green 3x.
title: No test guards against unreachable/unjustified callable facts in the product inventory
